LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 9.3.1 WORD CLASSES: ADVERBS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Word Classes: Adverbs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Word Classes: Adverbs. Read, look at the pictures, practise, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: LEARN

Welcome to an English program for grade four. Today, we are going to learn how to use constructed forms of verbs, positive and negative statement s. - Learner, I want you to listen to these sentences. My name is Cow. I can eat grass. But I cannot eat meat. My name is Cow. I can eat grass. But I cannot eat meat. My name is Hen. I have wings, but I do not have horns. My name is Hen. I have wings, but I do not have horns. Learner. Tell me something you cannot eat. - Tell me something you do not have. - Did you say I cannot eat snakes? I do not have money?. Those are good sentences. Learner I want you to write the following sentences in your exercise book. Number one, my name is Goat. My name is not Sheep. My name is Goat. My name is not sheep. - We are dogs. We are not wild animals. We are dogs. We are not wild animals. - I have wings, but I do not have horns. I have wings, but I do not have horns. - I can eat grass, but I cannot eat meat. I can eat grass, but I cannot eat meat.

Learner, look at the sentences you have written. One. My name is Goat. It is positive. My name is not sheep. That sentence is negative. Number two. We are dogs. That is a positive sentence. We are not wild animals. That is a negative sentence. Number three. I have wings. That is positive. But I do not have horns. That is negative. And number four. I can eat grass. Positive. But I cannot eat meat. That one is negative. Learner, look at the sentences you have written and underline the words. Is not. are not. Do not and cannot. Look at the sentences you have written and underline the words. Is not. are not. Do not and cannot. The underlined wordss can be made shorter. For example, number one. Instead of is not we may say isn't. isn't Number two. Instead of are not, we may say aren’t. aren’t. Number three. Instead of do not, we may say don't. don't. And number four, instead of cannot, we may say can't. can't. Learner in the contracted verbs, the letter “O” is removed. And an apostrophe is added. in the contracted verbs, the letter “O” is removed. And an apostrophe is added. Now spell the word isn't. Isn't. - Spell the word isn't. Isn't. The spelling is. I. S. N apostrophe. T. Now spell the word aren’t. The spelling is. A. R. E. N. apostrophe. T. Spell the word don’t. The spelling is. D. O. N. apostrophe. T.

And now spell the word can’t. The spelling is. C. A. N. apostrophe. T. Very good, Learner. Now, write down the contracted forms of the following sentences. Write down the contracted forms of the following sentences. Number one. I cannot sleep today. I cannot sleep today. Number two. I do not have books. I do not have books. Number three. My name is not Paul. My name is not Paul. And number four. We are not happy. We are not happy. Learner, did you get the following answers? Number one, I cannot sleep today. The contracted form is. I can't sleep today. Number two, I do not have books. The contracted form is. I don't have books. Number three. My name is not Paul. The contracted form is. My name isn't Paul. And number four, we are not happy. The contracted form is. We aren't happy. Learner, you at home assignment. Form your own sentences using the contracted forms Don't, Can't, Isn't and Aren’t. Share with your parent, sibling or caregiver. Thank you, learner. In our lesson today, we have learned how to use contracted forms of verbs correctly. - Your radio teacher was Joyce, Agik The program was written and produced by the It was recorded by John Mbithi for the Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development. Until next time, goodbye.

SECTION 3: TRY THIS

1. Look again at the examples or pictures above.
2. Tell a parent or friend what Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Word Classes: Adverbs means, using your own words.
3. Copy one example into your exercise book and change it to fit your school or home.
4. Underline three new words and find out what they mean.

SECTION 4: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Word Classes: Adverbs.
2. Complete any “Work to do” items shown in the pupil book pages above.
3. Create three of your own practice questions on this topic.
4. Answer the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after finishing.
